text:
Lena Ortiz: Hey team — we've been getting a surge of 429s since ~09:10 UTC. Traffic looks identical, same API key, but a subset of requests are failing with rate limit errors. Can someone check if this is quota, IP scoping, or billing?

Samira - Support: Sorry you're hitting that, Lena. Can you paste the exact error body you saw? Also which API key and whether you're going through a proxy?

Lena Ortiz: Error body: `\{"error\":\{"type\":\"rate_limit\",\"message\":\"Rate limit exceeded\",\"scope\":\"api_key\"\}}`. We're using key `rk-prod-abc123` behind a corporate proxy. Proxy rotates egress IPs.

Samira - Support: Thanks. Two quick things we'll check: 1) if the proxy rotation causes multiple IPs that hit an IP-based bucket, and 2) whether the key's project quota was exhausted. @Priya can you pull the rate limit logs for that key and recent IPs?

Priya - SRE: Pulling logs now. Found a pattern: bursts from two IPs (203.0.113.5, 198.51.100.12) around 09:08-09:12 UTC. Log sample:```[09:09:02] key=rk-prod-abc123 ip=203.0.113.5 status=429 reason=RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED scope=api_key bucket=per_minute```:message="tokens=300/300"
Also saw entries: `scope=ip bucket=per_minute tokens=30/30` for the other IP.

Dave K - Eng Platform: Quick note on scoping precedence: our enforcement checks (1) per-key quotas, (2) per-project quotas, (3) per-org quotas, and (4) IP-based buckets for egress. If any check fails we return a 429 and include the `scope` field that indicates which check triggered it. There's also a separate billing-hold throttle we apply when invoices are overdue that behaves like an org-level cap.

Lena Ortiz: Ah — our billing email bounced last week. Could that trigger the org-level throttle? Billing showed green in console though.

Billing Bot: Billing alert: account/redwood-acme has an overdue invoice (INV-2025-09). A temporary org-level softcap was applied 2025-09-12 02:34:11 UTC. Contact billing@redwood.ai to resolve.

Maya - ProdOps: If an org-level softcap is active it limits sustained throughput and also reduces burst allowance. But the `scope` in Lena's first sample shows `api_key`, so the key-level bucket hit first. That can happen even if org-level cap exists: both are checked and the first to be exceeded wins the error scope.

Samira - Support: Lena — can you confirm whether some traffic sources share that same API key? E.g., background jobs + front-end mobile?

Lena Ortiz: Yes — we have 3 services using rk-prod-abc123 (webhooks, ingestion, frontend). We recently rolled a batch job that spiked ingestion.

Priya - SRE: That explains the `tokens=300/300` in the per_minute key bucket. Two helpful repro steps: 1) run a controlled curl loop from one IP to see per-ip bucket behavior; 2) run the same loop using the API key from a single host to see key-level exhaustion. Example curl for repro:

```bash
for i in {1..350}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %time_total\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer rk-prod-abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
 done
```

You should see 200s until the bucket is exhausted and then 429s reporting `scope=api_key` or `scope=ip` depending on the host pattern.

Dave K - Eng Platform: A few edge-case notes to avoid confusion:
- IP-based limits apply to the egress IPs we see. If you run through a proxy that rewrites X-Forwarded-For, we use egress IP not XFF for rate enforcement.
- If you have multiple projects under the same org, per-project quotas are enforced separately but key-level quotas are tied to the project the key belongs to.
- Billing holds apply at the org level and will surface as `scope=org` when that check trips, but you'll still get `scope=api_key` if the API key bucket depletes first.

Lena Ortiz: Ok makes sense. So even with an overdue invoice, we can still hit key limits first. But why did some requests succeed while others failed if they share the same key?

Priya - SRE: Because your proxy rotates egress IPs. Some IPs still had available IP-bucket tokens and some didn't. Meanwhile the API key bucket was shared across all three services, so bursts from ingestion quickly consumed it. Interleaving can produce the observed mixed success.

Samira - Support: Actionable next steps for the customer:
1) Create service-specific API keys (one per service) so bursts are isolated.
2) Whitelist stable egress IPs or use a NAT with a fixed IP so you don't hit many IP buckets.
3) Resolve billing hold with Billing team to remove the org softcap.
4) If you need immediate capacity, we can temporarily raise the key and project bucket limits — @Dave can apply a short-lived bump.

Lena Ortiz: We can rotate keys but rolling out new keys to all services will take ~30m. Can we get the temporary bump?

Dave K - Eng Platform: I applied a temporary +3x per_minute bump to rk-prod-abc123 and a +2x to the project per_minute bucket for 60 minutes. Watch the logs; that'll let ingestion finish while you roll keys. I also added a note to engineering logs: `incident: temp-bump rk-prod-abc123 by eng-platform (expires in 3600s)`.

Priya - SRE: Confirmed — post-bump the 429 rate dropped dramatically. Sample log:```[09:20:01] key=rk-prod-abc123 ip=203.0.113.5 status=200 latency=0.24s```.

Billing Bot: Billing update: invoice INV-2025-09 marked paid 2025-09-12 09:25:00 UTC. Org softcap removed.

Lena Ortiz: All good now — 200s across the board. Thanks for the quick bump and the explanation.

Samira - Support: Glad it's resolved. We'll leave a short playbook here for you to avoid reoccurrence: 1) per-service keys, 2) fix proxy NAT, 3) set alerting on per-key consumption in Console (threshold 80%), 4) ensure billing emails are current. If you want we can convert this to a support plan item to rotate keys for you.

Lena Ortiz: Yes please — can someone open a ticket to rotate keys and add alerts?

Samira - Support: Opening a follow-up ticket and assigning to Eng Ops. Ticket: SUP-2025-4627.

Samira - Support: Closing thread — reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
